$$

$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=-\frac{{y}^{3}}{2y+16}.
$$

Finally, substituting the point $(3,2),$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(3,2)} & =-\frac{{2}^{3}}{2(2)+16} \\  & =-\frac{8}{20} \\  & =-\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given a curve $x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}-2{y}^{2},$ what is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $(-1,1)?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}-2{y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}})-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-1/2})-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{y}^{-3/2}-2\cdot (2y) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2{y}^{3/2}}-4y \\  & =\frac{-1-8{y}^{5/2}}{2{y}^{3/2}} \\  & =-\frac{1+8{y}^{2}\sqrt{y}}{2y\sqrt{y}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=-\frac{2y\sqrt{y}}{1+8{y}^{2}\sqrt{y}}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(-1,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(-1,1)} \\  & =-\frac{2(1)\sqrt{1}}{1+8(1)^{2}\sqrt{1}} \\  & =-\frac{2}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =-\frac{2}{9}(x-(-1)) \\ y & =-\frac{2}{9}x-\frac{2}{9}+1 \\ y & =-\frac{2}{9}x+\frac{7}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{2{y}^{2}-2y}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(9,3)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(9,3)} \\  & =\frac{1}{2(3)^{2}-2(3)} \\  & =\frac{1}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

questions.problem: Given a curve $x=4{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}-1,$ what is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $(4,1)?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(4{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}-1) \\  & =4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{1}{{y}^{2}})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(1) \\  & =4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(1) \\  & =4\cdot (2y)-2{y}^{-3}-0 \\  & =8y-\frac{2}{{y}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{8{y}^{4}-2}{{y}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{{y}^{3}}{8{y}^{4}-2}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(4,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(4,1)} \\  & =\frac{(1)^{3}}{8(1)^{4}-2} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =\frac{1}{6}(x-4) \\ y & =\frac{x}{6}-\frac{2}{3}+1 \\ y & =\frac{x}{6}+\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
